# tokenpony / Token Pony Express (TPX) v0.1

tokenpony is an LLM inference provider implementing TPX, an OAuth-style protocol where an
application ships with NO LLM credentials of its own. The end user grants the app a metered
credit budget from a provider the user chooses and pays. Grants are budget-capped,
revocable, and pseudonymous (they carry no user identity).

- Issuer (provider API): https://api.tokenpony.dev
- Discovery: GET https://api.tokenpony.dev/.well-known/tpx
- Human spec: https://tokenpony.dev/spec
- User dashboard (passkey login): https://api.tokenpony.dev/dashboard
- Demo TPX client app: https://ponychat.tokenpony.dev

## Units

All balances and budgets are CREDITS: 1 credit = US$0.000001 (so "$X per M tokens" equals
exactly X credits per token). Users buy credits at the dashboard via Stripe; packs start at
$1 = 1,000,000 credits. There are no free credits. Per-model prices (USD per M input /
cached input / output tokens) are published live on the models endpoint.

## Integrating an app (the TPX flow)

Step 0. Discover. All shapes below generalize to any TPX issuer; hard-code the flow, not
the vendor.

    GET {issuer}/.well-known/tpx
    -> {
      "tpx_version": "0.1",
      "issuer": "https://api.tokenpony.dev",
      "authorization_endpoint": "https://api.tokenpony.dev/tpx/authorize",
      "token_endpoint": "https://api.tokenpony.dev/tpx/token",
      "registration_endpoint": "https://api.tokenpony.dev/tpx/register",
      "api_base": "https://api.tokenpony.dev/v1",
      "models_endpoint": "https://api.tokenpony.dev/v1/models",
      "documentation": "https://tokenpony.dev/llms.txt"
    }

Step 1. Register your app once per issuer (open dynamic registration in v0.1). Store the
secret; it is shown once and held hashed server-side.

    POST {registration_endpoint}
    Content-Type: application/json
    { "name": "My App", "redirect_uris": ["https://myapp.example/callback"] }
    -> { "client_id": "app_...", "client_secret": "cs_..." }

    redirect_uris must be https (localhost allowed for development).

Step 2. Authorize. Send the user's browser to:

    {authorization_endpoint}?client_id=app_...
      &redirect_uri=https://myapp.example/callback   (must exactly match a registered URI)
      &state={opaque-csrf-value}                     (required; verify on return)
      &budget={credits}                              (integer 1..10000000, i.e. up to $10)

The provider authenticates the user (tokenpony uses passkeys via AuthGravity) and shows a
consent page with your app name and the requested budget. On approval:

    302 {redirect_uri}?code=tpxc_...&state={state}     (code is single-use, expires in 5 min)

On denial: 302 {redirect_uri}?error=access_denied&state={state}

Step 3. Exchange the code (server-side).

    POST {token_endpoint}
    Content-Type: application/json
    {
      "grant_type": "authorization_code",
      "code": "tpxc_...",
      "client_id": "app_...",
      "client_secret": "cs_...",
      "redirect_uri": "https://myapp.example/callback"
    }
    -> {
      "access_token": "tpx_...",
      "token_type": "bearer",
      "budget": 100000,
      "budget_used": 0,
      "api_base": "https://api.tokenpony.dev/v1"
    }

Step 4. Chat on the user's credits. api_base is OpenAI-compatible; any OpenAI SDK works by
setting baseURL={api_base} and apiKey={access_token}.

    GET  {api_base}/models          (no auth required; includes live per-model pricing)
    POST {api_base}/chat/completions
    Authorization: Bearer tpx_...
    { "model": "llama-3.3-70b", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],
      "stream": true|false, "max_tokens": 2048, "temperature": 0.7 }

Responses are standard OpenAI chat-completion shapes (SSE chunks when streaming). The
usage block is extended with the exact charge:

    "usage": {
      "prompt_tokens": 40, "completion_tokens": 3, "total_tokens": 43,
      "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 0 },
      "credits_charged": 19
    }

In streaming responses, usage arrives in the final chunk before "data: [DONE]".
max_tokens is automatically clamped to what the grant/balance can still afford.

## Errors

All errors: HTTP status + body { "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }

    401 invalid_token       unknown/malformed/revoked-and-purged token
    402 budget_exhausted    grant budget spent -> run the authorize flow again for a new grant
    402 balance_exhausted   the user's provider balance is empty -> user must top up
    403 grant_revoked       the user revoked this grant at the provider
    400 invalid_grant       bad/expired/reused authorization code
    404 model_not_found     unknown model id; list {models_endpoint}
    502 upstream_error      inference backend failure

When a grant runs dry, simply start a new authorization request; the user decides whether
to top the app up. Never ask users for provider API keys; that is what grants replace.

## Personal API keys (non-TPX path)

Users can mint personal keys (sk_...) in the dashboard and use them directly against
{api_base} with any OpenAI SDK. Same metering, same error shapes.

## Security notes

- Always send and verify the state parameter.
- Authorization codes are single-use with a 5-minute TTL.
- Tokens and client secrets are stored hashed by the provider.
- A grant is a damage cap: a leaked tpx_ token can spend at most the remaining budget and
  is revocable by the user at any time.
- Grants carry no user identity: no email, no name, no provider account id.
